transcription_notes: WITNESS: Cambridge University Library MS Add. 1570 (CAM), the second Samuel/Reigns witness, transcribed BLIND from the two ~7760x10328 hi-res stitched masters of f120r and f120v only. HAND & LAYOUT: a dense, regular, upright Ethiopic book hand, three columns per folio side (f120r columns at approx x 800-2350 / 2680-4180 / 4600-6110; f120v shifted right, columns at approx x 1900-3450 / 3800-5350 / 5750-7150; ~40-41 ruled lines per column). Heavy red rubrication: clause-initial words, divine names, the 'kefl' subdivision rubrics, and red cross-shaped clause dividers; the scribe also draws a curved seam-bracket flourish at major paragraph openings and uses superscript abbreviation strokes and small interlinear glosses. SEGMENTATION METHOD: the MS does not number verses; verses were segmented by the manuscript's own red cross sense-dividers plus narrative sense, numbered contiguously 1..26. KEFL CAUTION OBSERVED: the red 'kefl <numeral>' rubrics (kefl 30 at the 2 Sam 11 opening, kefl 31 at v2, kefl 32 near v13, kefl 34 at the 2 Sam 12 opening) are FINE LITURGICAL SUBDIVISIONS whose numerals climb fast within the chapter - they were explicitly NOT used to bound the chapter; the Bathsheba NARRATIVE was used to bound it. CAM also has no red cross between the material answering to the familiar v19 and v20, so those were merged into a single sense unit (object v=19) and the soft boundary flagged; the object numbering is therefore contiguous 1..26 (the familiar narrative's ~27 verses, with v19/20 as one unit). EXACT START LOCUS: 2 Sam 11:1 begins on f120r, column 2, line 8, at the red 'kefl 30' margin rubric with the curved seam-bracket, opening 'we-emz bedaha 0amete mawa'l ame ywede'u negest...' ('and it came to pass at the return of the year, when kings go forth...'). The end of 2 Sam 10 physically precedes it in col2 lines 1-7, concluding '...wa-ferhu Soreya ad0anotomu le-deqiqe Emon' ('and Syria feared to help the children of Ammon' = 2 Sam 10:19 end), preceded by the Aramean-war tally (David smote 600 of Syria, 40 charioteers, Shobach the captain died there, the servants of Hadadezer saw they were defeated before Israel). EXACT END LOCUS: 2 Sam 11 ends on f120v, column 1, line 6 into line 7, the final verse closing '...wakona zentu ekuye be-qedme Egzi'abher zegabra Dawit' ('but this thing that David had done was evil before the LORD') followed by a red cross. IMMEDIATELY after it, still on f120v col1 line 7, a red 'kefl 34' rubric plus curved seam-bracket introduces 2 Sam 12: 'wa-fenewo Egzi'abher le-Natan haba Dawit... helewu 2 0edew weste ahati hager 1 ba0l wa-1 neday... abaɠɠ wa-alhemt wa-le-neday... ahati beɠe0 enestit enta sayeta' (the LORD sends Nathan; two men in one city, one rich one poor, the rich man's many flocks and herds, the poor man's single little ewe-lamb). This 2 Sam 12 / Nathan / ewe-lamb material is the boundary proof and was EXCLUDED from this record. MARɠINAL/МЄ NOTE SITUATION: the upper running header of f120r reads a title plus a 'me0 14' (me'eraf ~14) chapter-style marginal numeral and the folio number '120'; within the text body the only marginalia are the red 'kefl' liturgical subdivision rubrics and small black interlinear scribal glosses/abbreviation-expansions (e.g. an 'Egzi'e' divine-name expansion glossed above f120r col3 L3, and an interpretive interlinear note between f120r col3 L40 and L41). No separate running 'me'eraf 11' in-text chapter heading was found at the v1 seam beyond the kefl rubric. RECENSION ASSESSMENT (honest): CAM presents the FULL / LONG Bathsheba narrative. All of the well-known ~27-verse account is present and in order - war season, David on the roof, Bathsheba daughter of Eliam wife of Uriah, take/lie/return, conception and message, Uriah summoned, the roof-door refusal and the ark/tents speech, the drinking, the death-letter by Uriah's hand, the ambush and Uriah's death, Joab's messenger and the Abimelech-son-of-Roboam/woman/millstone/Thebez coaching, David's 'the sword devours' reply, Bathsheba's mourning, the marriage and the son, and the closing 'evil before the LORD'. No verse-block is omitted; the only structural shortfall vs the familiar 27 is that CAM does not separate v19 from v20 (merged here). CAM is therefore long/full, not a short recension; it is NOT reshaped to any external count. LEXICAL/ORTHOɠRAPHIC ODDITIES kept verbatim and flagged: Joab as 'Iyab' (v1) alongside 'Iyo'ab' elsewhere; Uriah as 'Oryo'/'Oryob' (anomalous final -b in v15) and the gentilic as both 'Zetyawi' (v3) and 'Ketyawi'; Bathsheba 'Bersabeh', Eliam 'Elyab'; Rabbah 'Raba'; Thebez 'Tamnas'; Jerubbesheth replaced by 'walde Rob'am' (son of Roboam, a genuine recension variant); plus several defective spellings (hgar for hager, da0ana, serkeke, tekto-ha, etc.) all transcribed as seen and marked uncertain. A clear COLUMN-TURN DITTOɠRAPHY of 'ebew' occurs at the f120r col2->col3 boundary in v11 (written line-final on col2 L40 and again line-initial on col3 L1); both copies are transcribed and flagged, not corrected. Superscript abbreviation strokes (on Egzi'abher, iya0bes) and interlinear glosses are described here and flagged but the glosses are NOT merged into the geez. NUMERAL HANDLINɠ: no Ethiopic numeral glyph occurs inside the body of 2 Sam 11 itself; the numerals seen are the 2 Sam 10 war tallies (immediately before v1, excluded), the red 'kefl' subdivision numerals and a small red interlinear '40' near v20 (subdivision apparatus, not scripture text, so not tokenised), and the 2 Sam 12 numerals (excluded). No number was padded or converted; none needed standalone numeral tokens within the chapter. GEEZ/TOKEN CONVENTION: per the CAM template the geez strings KEEP the Ethiopic wordspace and the terminal/clausal full stop; the red cross dividers and kefl rubrics are STRIPPED from geez (they are liturgical punctuation, described here) and likewise absent from tokens; tokens are word-only. DAMAɠE/CONDITION: the parchment is clean and the ink generally excellent; no token is fully illegible, so the illegible-token count is 0 and the ⟦illegible⟧<->'illegible' correspondence holds 1:1 trivially (0 of each). Items marked 'damaged' (best reading proposed from context) are the faded brown 'be'sit' in v3, the abbreviated column-edge 'ebew' in v11, the rubbed 'em-ryo' in v20, and the abbreviated column-edge 'iya0bes' in v24; all remaining flags are 'uncertain' (legible-but-noted: orthography kept as seen, soft boundaries, dittography, name-forms, the v19/20 merge).
